sanskrit: vyākṣipann āyudhān anye mamṛduś cāpare bhujān anye cānvapatan droṇaṃ tyaktātmāno mahaujasaḥ
english: Some flung their weapons at him, others crushed his arms in their grip, and yet others, men of mighty vigor who had renounced all care for their lives, hurled themselves upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: pāñcālās tu viśeṣeṇa droṇasāyakapīḍitāḥ samasajjanta rājendra samare bhṛśavedanāḥ
english: The Pāñcālas above all, sorely afflicted by Droṇa's shafts and racked with anguish, closed with him in battle, O lord of kings.

sanskrit: tato virāṭadrupadau droṇaṃ pratiyayū raṇe tathā carantaṃ saṃgrāme bhṛśaṃ samaradurjayam
english: Then Virāṭa and Drupada advanced against Droṇa in the fight as he ranged through the conflict, well-nigh unconquerable in war.

sanskrit: drupadasya tataḥ pautrās traya eva viśāṃ pate cedayaś ca maheṣvāsā droṇam evābhyayur yudhi
english: Then the three grandsons of Drupada, O lord of peoples, and the mighty bowmen of the Cedis bore down upon Droṇa in battle.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ drupadapautrāṇāṃ trayāṇāṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ tribhir droṇo 'harat prāṇāṃs te hatā nyapatan bhuvi
english: With three whetted arrows Droṇa took the lives of those three grandsons of Drupada, and slain they fell to the earth.

sanskrit: tato droṇo 'jayad yuddhe cedikekayasṛñjayān matsyāṃś caivājayat sarvān bhāradvājo mahārathaḥ
english: Then Droṇa conquered in the fight the Cedis, the Kekayas, and the Sṛñjayas, and the great chariot-warrior, son of Bharadvāja, vanquished all the Matsyas as well.

sanskrit: tatas tu drupadaḥ krodhāc charavarṣam avākirat droṇaṃ prati mahārāja virāṭaś caiva saṃyuge
english: Then Drupada in his wrath poured down a rain of arrows upon Droṇa, O great king, and Virāṭa did likewise in the encounter.

sanskrit: tato droṇaḥ supītābhyāṃ bhallābhyām arimardanaḥ drupadaṃ ca virāṭaṃ ca praiṣīd vaivasvatakṣayam
english: Then Droṇa, crusher of foes, with two well-burnished broad-headed shafts dispatched both Drupada and Virāṭa to the abode of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: hate virāṭe drupade kekayeṣu tathaiva ca tathaiva cedimatsyeṣu pāñcāleṣu tathaiva ca hateṣu triṣu vīreṣu drupadasya ca naptṛṣu
english: When Virāṭa and Drupada were slain, and the Kekayas likewise, and the Cedis and Matsyas and Pāñcālas as well, and when the three heroes who were Drupada's grandsons had been killed—

sanskrit: droṇasya karma tad dṛṣṭvā kopaduḥkhasamanvitaḥ śaśāpa rathināṃ madhye dhṛṣṭadyumno mahāmanāḥ
english: beholding that deed of Droṇa, the high-minded Dhṛṣṭadyumna, filled with wrath and grief, swore an oath in the midst of the chariot-warriors:

sanskrit: iṣṭāpūrtāt tathā kṣātrād brāhmaṇyāc ca sa naśyatu droṇo yasyādya mucyeta yo vā droṇāt parāṅmukhaḥ
english: "Let that man fall from the merit of his sacrifices and pious works, from his Kṣatriya estate and his Brahmin standing, who today lets Droṇa go free, or who turns his back upon Droṇa."

sanskrit: iti teṣāṃ pratiśrutya madhye sarvadhanuṣmatām āyād droṇaṃ sahānīkaḥ pāñcālyaḥ paravīrahā pāñcālās tv ekato droṇam abhyaghnan pāṇḍavānyataḥ
english: Having thus pledged himself in the midst of all the bowmen, the Pāñcāla prince, slayer of enemy heroes, advanced upon Droṇa together with his host; the Pāñcālas struck at Droṇa from one side and the Pāṇḍavas from the other.

sanskrit: duryodhanaś ca karṇaś ca śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ sodaryāś ca yathā mukhyās te 'rakṣan droṇam āhave
english: And Duryodhana and Karṇa, and Śakuni the son of Subala, and his foremost brothers—these guarded Droṇa in the battle.

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇaṃ tathā droṇaṃ samare tair mahātmabhiḥ yatamānāpi pāñcālā na śekuḥ prativīkṣitum
english: Droṇa being thus guarded in the fray by those great-souled warriors, the Pāñcālas, strive as they might, could not so much as look upon him.

sanskrit: tatrākrudhyad bhīmaseno dhṛṣṭadyumnasya māriṣa sa enaṃ vāgbhir ugrābhis tatakṣa puruṣarṣabha
english: Thereupon Bhīmasena grew angry with Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O venerable one, and that bull among men cut him with harsh words:

sanskrit: drupadasya kule jātaḥ sarvāstreṣv astravittamaḥ kaḥ kṣatriyo manyamānaḥ prekṣetārim avasthitam
english: "Born in the line of Drupada, most learned in all weapons—what Kṣatriya worthy of the name would stand and merely gaze upon his foe before him?

sanskrit: pitṛputravadhaṃ prāpya pumān kaḥ parihāpayet viśeṣatas tu śapathaṃ śapitvā rājasaṃsadi
english: Having suffered the slaying of his father and his sons, what man would let the matter slip—above all after swearing an oath in the assembly of kings?

sanskrit: eṣa vaiśvānara iva samiddhaḥ svena tejasā śaracāpendhano droṇaḥ kṣatraṃ dahati tejasā
english: Like the fire of Vaiśvānara kindled bright by its own splendor, this Droṇa, with bow and arrows for his fuel, consumes the Kṣatriya host with his blazing might.

sanskrit: purā karoti niḥśeṣāṃ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm sthitāḥ paśyata me karma droṇam eva vrajāmy aham
english: Before he leaves the army of the Pāṇḍavas without a remnant—stand and watch my deed: I go straight against Droṇa myself."

sanskrit: ity uktvā prāviśat kruddho droṇānīkaṃ vṛkodaraḥ dṛḍhaiḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭair drāvayaṃs tava vāhinīm
english: Having spoken thus, Vṛkodara in his wrath plunged into Droṇa's division, scattering your army with firm shafts loosed from a bow drawn to the full.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno 'pi pāñcālyaḥ praviśya mahatīṃ camūm āsasāda raṇe droṇaṃ tadāsīt tumulaṃ mahat
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna the Pāñcāla too, breaking into the great host, came upon Droṇa in the fight; and then a great tumult arose.

sanskrit: naiva nas tādṛśaṃ yuddhaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ na ca śrutam yathā sūryodaye rājan samutpiñjo 'bhavan mahān
english: Never before had we seen or heard of such a battle as this, O king: at sunrise a great confusion arose.

sanskrit: saṃsaktāni vyadṛśyanta rathavṛndāni māriṣa hatāni ca vikīrṇāni śarīrāṇi śarīriṇām
english: Throngs of chariots were seen locked together, O venerable one, and the bodies of the slain lay scattered all about.

sanskrit: ke cid anyatra gacchantaḥ pathi cānyair upadrutāḥ vimukhāḥ pṛṣṭhataś cānye tāḍyante pārśvato 'pare
english: Some, making their way elsewhere, were set upon by others on the road; some who had turned away were struck from behind, and others were struck upon the flank.

sanskrit: tathā saṃsaktayuddhaṃ tad abhavad bhṛśadāruṇam atha saṃdhyāgataḥ sūryaḥ kṣaṇena samapadyata
english: So that close-grappled fighting grew exceedingly terrible; and presently the sun reached the twilight hour.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca te tathaiva mahārāja daṃśitā raṇamūrdhani saṃdhyāgataṃ sahasrāṃśum ādityam upatasthire
english: Saṃjaya said: Even so, O great king, those warriors in their armor, at the forefront of battle, did homage to the thousand-rayed sun as it came to the hour of twilight.

sanskrit: udite tu sahasrāṃśau taptakāñcanasaprabhe prakāśiteṣu lokeṣu punar yuddham avartata
english: But when the thousand-rayed one rose again, gleaming like molten gold, and the worlds were lit with its light, the battle was renewed.

sanskrit: dvaṃdvāni yāni tatrāsan saṃsaktāni purodayāt tāny evābhyudite sūrye samasajjanta bhārata
english: Those single combats which had been joined there before the dawn, O Bhārata, were taken up afresh when the sun had risen.

sanskrit: rathair hayā hayair nāgāḥ pādātāś cāpi kuñjaraiḥ hayā hayaiḥ samājagmuḥ pādātāś ca padātibhiḥ saṃsaktāś ca viyuktāś ca yodhāḥ saṃnyapatan raṇe
english: Horses met chariots, elephants met horses, foot-soldiers met the great tuskers, horse closed with horse and foot-soldier with foot-soldier; and the warriors, locked together and torn apart, fell upon one another in the battle.

sanskrit: te rātrau kṛtakarmāṇaḥ śrāntāḥ sūryasya tejasā kṣutpipāsāparītāṅgā visaṃjñā bahavo 'bhavan
english: Spent with their night-long labors, and now scorched by the sun's heat, their limbs beset by hunger and thirst, many of them swooned away.

sanskrit: śaṅkhabherīmṛdaṅgānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca garjatām visphāritavikṛṣṭānāṃ kārmukāṇāṃ ca kūjatām
english: Of the conches, kettledrums, and tabors, of the trumpeting elephants, and of the bows stretched wide and twanging—

sanskrit: śabdaḥ samabhavad rājan divispṛg bharatarṣabha dravatāṃ ca padātīnāṃ śastrāṇāṃ vinipātyatām
english: a din arose, O king, that touched the very heavens, O bull of the Bhāratas—the noise of fleeing foot-soldiers and of weapons hurled down,

sanskrit: hayānāṃ heṣatāṃ caiva rathānāṃ ca nivartatām krośatāṃ garjatāṃ caiva tadāsīt tumulaṃ mahat
english: of horses neighing and chariots wheeling about, of men crying out and roaring—and a great tumult arose.

sanskrit: vivṛddhas tumulaḥ śabdo dyām agacchan mahāsvanaḥ nānāyudhanikṛttānāṃ ceṣṭatām āturaḥ svanaḥ
english: Swelling ever greater, the tumultuous roar mounted to the sky in a mighty voice; and the anguished cries of those mangled by manifold weapons, writhing where they lay,

sanskrit: bhūmāv aśrūyata mahāṃs tadāsīt kṛpaṇaṃ mahat patatāṃ patitānāṃ ca pattyaśvarathahastinām
english: were heard loud upon the earth; and great was the misery then—of foot-soldiers, horses, chariots, and elephants falling and fallen.

sanskrit: teṣu sarveṣv anīkeṣu vyatiṣakteṣv anekaśaḥ sve svāñ jaghnuḥ pare svāṃś ca sve parāṃś ca parān pare
english: As all those hosts became entangled together in countless ways, one's own struck down one's own, foes struck one's own, one's own struck foes, and foes struck foes.

sanskrit: vīrabāhuvisṛṣṭāś ca yodheṣu ca gajeṣu ca asayaḥ pratyadṛśyanta vāsasāṃ nejaneṣv iva
english: Swords loosed by the arms of heroes flashed among the warriors and the elephants like washermen's paddles at the washing of garments.

sanskrit: udyatapratipiṣṭānāṃ khaḍgānāṃ vīrabāhubhiḥ sa eva śabdas tadrūpo vāsasāṃ nijyatām iva
english: Of the blades raised high and beaten together by the arms of heroes there came that very sound, as of garments being pounded at the wash.

sanskrit: ardhāsibhis tathā khaḍgais tomaraiḥ saparaśvadhaiḥ nikṛṣṭayuddhaṃ saṃsaktaṃ mahad āsīt sudāruṇam
english: With half-swords and broadswords, with lances and battle-axes, a great close-quarters fight was joined, hand to hand and exceedingly terrible.

sanskrit: gajāśvakāyaprabhavāṃ naradehapravāhinīm śastramatsyasusaṃpūrṇāṃ māṃsaśoṇitakardamām
english: Rising from the bodies of elephants and horses, bearing along the corpses of men, well filled with weapons for its fish, its mire made of flesh and blood,

sanskrit: ārtanādasvanavatīṃ patākāvastraphenilām nadīṃ prāvartayan vīrāḥ paralokapravāhinīm
english: loud with the cries of the stricken, foaming with banners and garments—such a river the heroes set flowing, that bore men onward to the other world.

sanskrit: śaraśaktyarditāḥ klāntā rātrimūḍhālpacetasaḥ viṣṭabhya sarvagātrāṇi vyatiṣṭhan gajavājinaḥ saṃśuṣkavadanā vīrāḥ śirobhiś cārukuṇḍalaiḥ
english: Tormented by arrows and spears, worn out, their wits dulled and bewildered by the night, the elephants and horses stood there, bracing every limb; and the heroes, their faces parched, with their heads adorned by lovely earrings—

sanskrit: yuddhopakaraṇaiś cānyais tatra tatra prakāśitaiḥ kravyādasaṃghair ākīrṇaṃ mṛtair ardhamṛtair api nāsīd rathapathas tatra sarvam āyodhanaṃ prati
english: and with the other implements of war glittering here and there, with the dead and the half-dead, and thronged by packs of carrion-eaters, the whole battlefield was so strewn that there was no path left for a chariot anywhere upon it.

sanskrit: majjatsu cakreṣu rathān sattvam āsthāya vājinaḥ kathaṃ cid avahañ śrāntā vepamānāḥ śarārditāḥ kulasattvabalopetā vājino vāraṇopamāḥ
english: As the wheels sank deep, the horses—mustering their spirit—somehow dragged the chariots on, weary, trembling, tormented by arrows, those steeds endowed with good breeding, mettle, and strength, the equals of elephants.

sanskrit: vihvalaṃ tat samudbhrāntaṃ sabhayaṃ bhāratāturam balam āsīt tadā sarvam ṛte droṇārjunāv ubhau
english: All that host, O Bhārata, was then reeling, frenzied, fearful, and distressed—save only those two, Droṇa and Arjuna.

sanskrit: tāv evāstāṃ nilayanaṃ tāv ārtāyanam eva ca tāv evānye samāsādya jagmur vaivasvatakṣayam
english: They two were the refuge, they two the recourse of the afflicted; yet others, approaching those two, went only to the abode of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: āvignam abhavat sarvaṃ kauravāṇāṃ mahad balam pāñcālānāṃ ca saṃsaktaṃ na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: The whole great army of the Kauravas was thrown into confusion, and so too the host of the Pāñcālas locked with it; nothing whatever could be made out.

sanskrit: antakākrīḍasadṛśe bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhane pṛthivyāṃ rājavaṃśānām utthite mahati kṣaye
english: As that great destruction of the royal houses arose upon the earth—like the playground of Death, swelling the terror of the timid—

sanskrit: na tatra karṇaṃ na droṇaṃ nārjunaṃ na yudhiṣṭhiram na bhīmasenaṃ na yamau na pāñcālyaṃ na sātyakim
english: there neither Karṇa nor Droṇa, neither Arjuna nor Yudhiṣṭhira, neither Bhīmasena nor the twins, neither the Pāñcāla prince nor Sātyaki,

sanskrit: na ca duḥśāsanaṃ drauṇiṃ na duryodhanasaubalau na kṛpaṃ madrarājaṃ vā kṛtavarmāṇam eva ca
english: nor Duḥśāsana, nor Droṇa's son, nor Duryodhana and the son of Subala, nor Kṛpa, nor the king of the Madras, nor even Kṛtavarman—

sanskrit: na cānyān naiva cātmānaṃ na kṣitiṃ na diśas tathā paśyāma rājan saṃsaktān sainyena rajasāvṛtān
english: nor any others, nor even our own selves, nor the earth, nor the quarters of the sky—none of these could we see, O king, all locked in the press of the host and veiled in dust.

sanskrit: saṃbhrānte tumule ghore rajomeghe samutthite dvitīyām iva saṃprāptām amanyanta niśāṃ tadā
english: When the whirling, dreadful tumult arose and a cloud of dust mounted up, men deemed that a second night had come upon them.

sanskrit: na jñāyante kauraveyā na pāñcālā na pāṇḍavāḥ na diśo na divaṃ norvīṃ na samaṃ viṣamaṃ tathā
english: The Kauravas were not to be known, nor the Pāñcālas, nor the Pāṇḍavas; neither the quarters, nor the sky, nor the earth, nor level ground from broken could be told apart.

sanskrit: hastasaṃsparśam āpannān parān vāpy atha vā svakān nyapātayaṃs tadā yuddhe narāḥ sma vijayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Whomever came within the touch of their hands, whether foe or even one of their own, the men, eager for victory, struck down in that battle.

sanskrit: uddhūtatvāt tu rajasaḥ prasekāc choṇitasya ca praśaśāma rajo bhaumaṃ śīghratvād anilasya ca
english: But because the dust had been thrown up, and through the sprinkling of blood, and through the swiftness of the wind, the dust of the earth was laid.

sanskrit: tatra nāgā hayā yodhā rathino 'tha padātayaḥ pārijātavanānīva vyarocan rudhirokṣitāḥ
english: There the elephants, horses, warriors, chariot-fighters, and foot-soldiers, drenched in blood, shone like groves of pārijāta in flower.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ karṇo droṇo duḥśāsanas tathā pāṇḍavaiḥ samasajjanta caturbhiś caturo rathāḥ
english: Then Duryodhana, Karṇa, Droṇa, and Duḥśāsana—four chariot-warriors—closed in combat with four of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: duryodhanaḥ saha bhrātrā yamābhyāṃ samasajjata vṛkodareṇa rādheyo bhāradvājena cārjunaḥ
english: Duryodhana with his brother engaged the twins, Rādheya engaged Vṛkodara, and Arjuna engaged the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: tad ghoraṃ mahad āścaryaṃ sarve praikṣan samantataḥ ratharṣabhāṇām ugrāṇāṃ saṃnipātam amānuṣam
english: That dread and mighty marvel all beheld on every side—the superhuman clash of those fierce bulls among chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: rathamārgair vicitraiś ca vicitrarathasaṃkulam apaśyan rathino yuddhaṃ vicitraṃ citrayodhinām
english: With their varied chariot-courses, all crowded with wondrous cars, the chariot-fighters watched the marvelous battle of those warriors who fought in marvelous ways.

sanskrit: yatamānāḥ parākrāntāḥ parasparajigīṣavaḥ jīmūtā iva gharmānte śaravarṣair avākiran
english: Straining and valorous, each longing to overcome the other, they showered down their rains of arrows like thunderclouds at the close of the hot season.

sanskrit: te rathān sūryasaṃkāśān āsthitāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ aśobhanta yathā meghāḥ śāradāḥ samupasthitāḥ
english: Mounted upon their chariots bright as the sun, those bulls among men shone like autumn clouds drawn up together.

sanskrit: spardhinas te maheṣvāsāḥ kṛtayatnā dhanurdharāḥ abhyagacchaṃs tathānyonyaṃ mattā gajavṛṣā iva
english: Those rival mighty bowmen, putting forth their utmost effort, the bearers of the bow, went at one another like rutting bull-elephants.

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ dehabhedo 'sti kāle tasmin samāgate yatra sarve na yugapad vyaśīryanta mahārathāḥ
english: Surely the body knows no breaking when its appointed hour has not yet come—for there not all those great chariot-warriors perished together at once.

sanskrit: bāhubhiś caraṇaiś chinnaiḥ śirobhiś cārukuṇḍalaiḥ kārmukair viśikhaiḥ prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paraśupaṭṭiśaiḥ
english: With severed arms and legs, with heads adorned by lovely earrings, with bows, arrows, javelins, swords, axes, and spears,

sanskrit: nālīkakṣuranārācair nakharaiḥ śaktitomaraiḥ anyaiś ca vividhākārair dhautaiḥ praharaṇottamaiḥ
english: with nālīka shafts, razor-edged and iron arrows, with claw-spikes, lances, and pikes, and with other excellent burnished weapons of manifold forms,

sanskrit: citraiś ca vividhākāraiḥ śarīrāvaraṇair api vicitraiś ca rathair bhagnair hataiś ca gajavājibhiḥ
english: with bright body-armor of many shapes, with wondrous chariots shattered, and with slain elephants and horses,

sanskrit: śūnyaiś ca nagarākārair hatayodhadhvajai rathaiḥ amanuṣyair hayais trastaiḥ kṛṣyamāṇais tatas tataḥ
english: with empty chariots vast as towns, their warriors slain and their banners cut down, and with riderless, terrified horses dragging them this way and that,

sanskrit: vātāyamānair asakṛd dhatavīrair alaṃkṛtaiḥ vyajanaiḥ kaṅkaṭaiś caiva dhvajaiś ca vinipātitaiḥ
english: with steeds running swift as the wind again and again, decked out yet their heroes slain, with fans and coats of mail and banners fallen down,

sanskrit: chatrair ābharaṇair vastrair mālyaiś ca susugandhibhiḥ hāraiḥ kirīṭair mukuṭair uṣṇīṣaiḥ kiṅkiṇīgaṇaiḥ
english: with parasols, ornaments, garments, and sweetly fragrant garlands, with necklaces, diadems, crowns, turbans, and clusters of little bells,

sanskrit: urasyair maṇibhir niṣkaiś cūḍāmaṇibhir eva ca āsīd āyodhanaṃ tatra nabhas tārāgaṇair iva
english: with breast-jewels, golden ornaments, and crest-gems, the battlefield there was strewn as the sky is strewn with the host of stars.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanasyāsīn nakulena samāgamaḥ amarṣitena kruddhasya kruddhenāmarṣitasya ca
english: Then there came an encounter between Duryodhana and Nakula—the one wrathful and indignant, the other indignant and wrathful.

sanskrit: apasavyaṃ cakārātha mādrīputras tavātmajam kirañ śaraśatair hṛṣṭas tatra nādo mahān abhūt
english: Then the son of Mādrī wheeled rightward about your son, joyfully scattering arrows by the hundred; and a great roar went up at that.

sanskrit: apasavyaṃ kṛtaḥ saṃkhye bhrātṛvyenātyamarṣiṇā so 'marṣitas tam apy ājau praticakre 'pasavyataḥ
english: Circled rightward in the battle by his exceedingly indignant cousin, he too in his indignation wheeled rightward about him in turn.

sanskrit: tataḥ praticikīrṣantam apasavyaṃ tu te sutam nyavārayata tejasvī nakulaś citramārgavit
english: But as your son sought to wheel rightward in return, the brilliant Nakula, skilled in wondrous maneuvers, held him back.

sanskrit: sarvato vinivāryainaṃ śarajālena pīḍayan vimukhaṃ nakulaś cakre tat sainyāḥ samapūjayan
english: Checking him on every side and pressing him with a net of arrows, Nakula made him turn away; and the soldiers applauded that feat.

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti nakulo babhāṣe tanayaṃ tava saṃsmṛtya sarvaduḥkhāni tava durmantritena ca
english: "Stand, stand!" cried Nakula to your son, calling to mind all the sorrows brought about by your ill counsel.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato duḥśāsanaḥ kruddhaḥ sahadevam upādravat rathavegena tīvreṇa kampayann iva medinīm
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Duḥśāsana in his wrath rushed upon Sahadeva, all but making the earth tremble with the fierce speed of his chariot.

sanskrit: tasyāpatata evāśu bhallenāmitrakarśanaḥ mādrīsutaḥ śiro yantuḥ saśirastrāṇam acchinat
english: As he bore swiftly down, the son of Mādrī, that scourge of foes, with a broad-headed shaft severed the head of his charioteer, helmet and all.

sanskrit: nainaṃ duḥśāsanaḥ sūtaṃ nāpi kaś cana sainikaḥ hṛtottamāṅgam āśutvāt sahadevena buddhavān
english: Neither Duḥśāsana nor any soldier marked that the charioteer's head had been struck off by Sahadeva, so swiftly was it done.
